questions.stem: A student calculates that a reaction should produce 10 g of product (theoretical yield), but only obtains 7.5 g (actual yield). What is the percentage yield?
questions.explanation: Percentage yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) x 100 = (7.5 / 10) x 100 = 75%. The percentage yield tells you the efficiency of a reaction. It is always 100% or less because you can never make more product than the theoretical maximum (conservation of mass).

questions.stem: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 56 g and a percentage yield of 80%. What is the actual mass of product obtained?
questions.explanation: Rearranging the formula: actual yield = (percentage yield / 100) x theoretical yield = (80/100) x 56 = 0.8 x 56 = 44.8 g. The actual yield is always less than the theoretical yield when percentage yield is below 100%.

questions.stem: Why is the percentage yield of a reaction usually less than 100%?

options.text: Because some mass is always converted to energy
Because atoms are lost during the reaction
Because of product loss during transfer, incomplete reactions, or side reactions
Because the balanced equation is always wrong

questions.explanation: Percentage yield is less than 100% for practical reasons: some product may be lost when transferring between containers, the reaction may not go to completion (reversible reactions), side reactions may produce unwanted products, or impure reactants may reduce the yield. Atoms are never actually lost or converted to energy in chemical reactions.

questions.stem: In the reaction CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂, 50 g of CaCO₃ should produce 28 g of CaO. The actual yield was 21 g. What was the percentage yield?
questions.explanation: Percentage yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) x 100 = (21 / 28) x 100 = 75%. The theoretical yield (28 g) was calculated from stoichiometry and represents the maximum possible product. The actual yield (21 g) is what was actually obtained in the experiment.

questions.stem: A pharmaceutical company needs 500 g of a drug. The synthesis has a percentage yield of 62.5%. What mass of theoretical product must the reaction be designed to produce?
questions.explanation: Rearranging: theoretical yield = actual yield / (percentage yield / 100) = 500 / 0.625 = 800 g. The company needs to design a reaction that theoretically produces 800 g, because at 62.5% yield, only 500 g will actually be obtained. This has important implications for cost and waste in industry.
